subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: What trusted/untrusted precedence and enforcement boundary should OpenClaw use when SKILL.md content becomes model-visible or slash-invoked?
rationale: The fix defines public security semantics across prompt precedence, skill metadata, memory influence, tool authority, sandbox/profile behavior, and upgrade compatibility, so automation should not choose that boundary alone.

options.title: Design The Boundary First
options.body: Define the skill precedence and capability contract, then implement enforcement and regression tests against that approved design.

options.title: Land Partial Mitigations
options.body: Treat Markdown scanning or inspect-only capability manifests as defense-in-depth while keeping this broader isolation issue open for runtime enforcement.

options.title: Defer Runtime Enforcement
options.body: Keep current visibility and scanning controls for now and revisit role, tool, and memory enforcement as part of a larger security-profile program.

recommendation.title: Design The Boundary First
recommendation.body: Define the skill precedence and capability contract, then implement enforcement and regression tests against that approved design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided security-review context on this issue and has the strongest adjacent history across skills prompt behavior and tests.
